articles.headline: At least 19 dead in stampede at Kolkata Hindu festival
keyFacts: At least 19 people died in a stampede during a Hindu festival in Kolkata, India, according to reports.
A seven-year-old girl was among the dead, and another 25 people were injured in the incident.
Heavy rain and a sudden crowd surge triggered the deadly crush.
body: At least 19 dead in stampede at Kolkata Hindu festival

A seven-year-old girl was among at least 19 people killed in a stampede during a Hindu festival in Kolkata, India. Heavy rain and a sudden crowd surge triggered the deadly crush, leaving another 25 people injured.

articles.headline: College football bowl projections: Slotting all 46 games after Week 7's historic run of upsets
keyFacts: Historic upsets in Week 7 of college football shook up playoff brackets and bowl projections, with multiple SEC teams projected to finish with three losses.
Auburn defeated Georgia on the road in a notable upset, while teams like Penn State and Oklahoma suffered damaging losses that hurt their postseason standing.
CBS Sports projected matchups for all 46 bowl games, including the College Football Playoff bracket featuring teams like Alabama, UCLA, Kentucky, and Ole Miss.
body: No wonder the SEC finally jumped on board for a which may come as soon as the 2027 season. For the first time in the CFP era, we expect at least two -- perhaps several -- three-loss SEC teams in the bracket this season, as chaos continued within the conference in Week 7.

Ranked No. 1 and unbeaten two weeks ago, , which came before top-ranked and Alabama lost at Tennessee, three of many stunning results across college football that shook up this week's bracket and bowl projections.

Theoretically, this is what we could be looking at in the SEC over the second half of the season leading into the CFP selection committee's final rankings during conference championship weekend. These are projected final records, not where these teams stand entering Week 8:
- Georgia 10-2
- Tennessee 10-2
- Ole Miss 10-2
- Alabama 9-3
- Kentucky 9-3
- LSU 9-3
- Texas 9-3
- Florida 9-3
- Missouri 8-4

Good luck determining the league tiebreaker on who gets to play Georgia in the SEC Championship Game, the last of its kind if we move to a 24-team playoff next fall. There's going to be a handful of SEC teams crying at the selection committee for not getting in this season, but there aren't enough spots to keep everyone who answers to Greg Sankey happy.
Ah, this season has truly been exhilarating, and we're only halfway through.

Here's an easy 250-mile trek to Frisco for Texas State, which crossed the 60-point plateau for the second time this season during Thursday's 66-27 victory over Colorado State. USF would much rather play in the Gasparilla Bowl, a home game for the Bulls, despite recent attendance issues at Raymond James Stadium. Next season, USF is expected to open their new 35,000-seat on-campus venue.

Projection: Western Michigan vs. Appalachian State

The Mountaineers erased a 10-point deficit to spoil Coastal Carolina's "90s Night" on Friday, pushing to 1-1 in the Sun Belt ahead of this week's Thursday night showdown against unbeaten JMU. There's a chance the Dukes (7-0) will be ranked when they travel to Boone, N.C. for one of the Group of Six's most important games left this season.
Gasparilla
Projection: Virginia vs. Texas A&M

Tampa in December probably wasn't what Texas A&M had in mind when this season began. A potential Gasparilla Bowl matchup with Virginia would be disappointing for a program spending too much money to settle for this destination. That's the uncomfortable reality facing Mike Elko, whose Aggies have dropped three of their four SEC games as after starting the season in the top 10.

FIU finishes out its three-game stretch of mid-week games on Tuesday against Middle Tennessee, a majority opportunity at home against a fellow 3-3 Conference USA opponent. Last week's 27-24 loss at Jacksonville State wasn't fatal to the Panthers' league title hopes, but it hurts. The Gamecocks are now unbeaten in conference play with a favorable remaining slate.
Independence
Projection: Iowa State vs. UConn

The Cyclones are 3-3 at midseason, but all three losses were to top-20 teams. With only one ranked opponent left, Iowa State's in a great position to finish strong and get to bowl eligibility. UConn's postseason trek begins next week at home against UMass in a Friday night affair. After that, tough matchups against Air Force, North Carolina and JMU could push the Huskies on the threshold of missing out unless they finish strong.
New Orleans
Projection: James Madison vs. Jacksonville State

JMU probably needs Boise State to suffer another loss to have a real shot at reaching the College Football Playoff for a second straight season. Oregon State, if it wins out, could have an argument, too. The Dukes handled Georgia State for their seventh straight win to open Bill Napier's first season, but are not going to have the strength of schedule compared to Boise State.

No projections are safe for the Nittany Lions, who dropped to 0-4 in Big Ten play and 3-4 overall after Saturday's loss at Michigan. Few expected Penn State to take three steps back under its new regime, but the schedule does lighten up from here with Purdue, Rutgers and Maryland among the final five opponents. Considering Penn State's one of only two Big Ten teams to miss Ohio State, Indiana and Oregon this fall, the 2026 campaign feels like a massive letdown.

Projection: Virginia Tech vs. Northwestern

The Hokies under first-year coach James Franklin snapped a two-game skid in the ACC against Georgia Tech and now have realistic hopes of getting to eight wins this fall and a quality bowl invite. Trips to SMU, Clemson and Miami remain for a team that has found an offensive rhythm behind Penn State transfer quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer and sophomore running back Jeffrey Overton Jr.

The Wolverines finally have a Big Ten win and may have a new quarterback, too. Tommy Carr led multiple touchdown drives in the second half of Michigan's victory over Penn State, delivering the final blow himself on a scoring scamper. He executed Jason Beck's offense with intention and moved ahead of the struggling Bryce Underwood in the process.
Birmingham
Projection: South Carolina vs. Pittsburgh

Left for dead at 0-3 in the SEC a few weeks ago, South Carolina responded with a blowout win at Florida and used its open date to recover from early-season injuries ahead of next weekend's home bout with Tennessee. From outside the bowl picture in September to the schedule not appearing as daunting, Shane Beamer has alleviated much of the job heat and should be able to get to bowl eligibility.

The Alamo Bowl gets its pick of teams from a pair of pools -- the Big 12 and the Pac-12/former Pac-12. It would be hard to pass up an opportunity to get the Utes and Ducks here if they're available. Unbeaten after Week 7, Utah remains in an ideal CFP position nearing the final month. The Utes host Houston next week and travel to Cincinnati before their game of the year against BYU. For now, as the games at BYU and at Arizona the following week. That would mean the Utes land at 10-2 overall here.

Projection: Duke vs. LSU

The Tigers control their own CFP destiny. However, they still have to go to Auburn next week, host Alabama, Texas and travel to Tennessee. Can LSU win all four of those games? Those squads are just as hungry to stay in the CFP picture, too. The bad news is LSU currently loses the "tiebreaker" of sorts with Ole Miss and Kentucky if all three of those teams finish with the same record and similar resumes.
Music City
Projection: Wisconsin vs. Auburn

Another week, another No. 1 team going down. This time, it was Auburn's road heroics at Georgia thanks to tough, between-the-tackle running from Byrum Brown and a couple timely stops defensively. Alex Golesh said after the game that he is rebuilding the Tigers into a national power, and the win over the Bulldogs was the first step toward that goal.
ReliaQuest
Projection: Nebraska vs. Mississippi State

It's a tough ask for Mississippi State to win a conference game on the road without Kamario Taylor and Fluff Bothwell. Mississippi State should still be ranked in Sunday's updated top 25, but it feels like CFP hopes are all but over for a squad with games remaining against Oklahoma, Texas and Ole Miss.
Sun
Projection: Clemson vs. Washington
Las Vegas
Projection: Arizona vs. Oklahoma

All the Sooners wanted was a chance, and they got the football back twice in the fourth quarter down a point against Kentucky, but couldn't manufacture points in a deflating 21-13 loss that included a late pick-six by the Wildcats off John Mateer. Coming off the program's win over then No. 1 Texas in Dallas, Oklahoma never found a rhythm offensively. Now at 3-3 overall, the alternating wins and losses won't cut it as far as CFP hopes are concerned.
Texas
Projection: Houston vs. Texas

Could the CFP selection committee leave the Longhorns out again? This time despite a huge nonconference victory over Ohio State? It's plausible if Texas finishes 9-3 and there are a couple of one-loss Big Ten at-large possibilities. Looking at you, Iowa and UCLA. Neither of those two teams would have as many quality wins as the Longhorns, but strength of record could outweigh conference strength. Truthfully, Texas simply isn't playing well enough right now to get to nine wins with what's left on the slate, not to mention quarterback issues and the injury to Colin Simmons.
Citrus
Projection: Iowa vs. Florida

Like UCLA, Iowa's journey to a potential 11-1 finish and an unexpected trip to the Big Ten Championship could certainly happen with Ohio State banged up and Indiana already saddled with a loss in conference play. However, we think the Hawkeyes lose another game somewhere.

Credit to Jon Sumrall's team for not backing down despite trailing by 14 points at Texas during the first half. They wilted under pressure the previous two weeks before posting their second win of the season against a top-10 opponent. Instead of a three-game skid entering the open date before Georgia, Florida should be back in the top-25 after the win and is very much alive in the CFP discussion. The consolation prize would be a short trek from Gainesville to Orlando if the Gators fail to get in. What a wild year thus far in the SEC.
First Responder
Projection: Florida State vs. Minnesota
Liberty
Projection: Oklahoma State vs. Missouri

Oklahoma State's loss to Houston all but assures the Cowboys won't make the Big 12 Championship Game. Missouri will enter its bye week needing to win out and finish 10-2 to secure a playoff berth. With games against top-15s Texas, Georgia and Kentucky left, the opportunity is there, but it's quite a mountain to climb.
Arizona
Projection: Ohio vs. Wyoming
Holiday
Projection: Wake Forest vs. USC

USC's date with Ohio State in two weeks doesn't look as daunting as it once did if Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin is unavailable, but that one lacks as much meaning if the Trojans fail to show at Wisconsin next week. Road games in the Big Ten have been a chore for this staff, and the Badgers are much improved after seeing their four-game winning streak snapped at UCLA in Week 7.
College Football Playoff
First round
Projection: (9) Alabama at (8) UCLA

One of five SEC teams in our new projection, Alabama's game at LSU on Nov. 7 could be for one of the final spots in the bracket. Consecutive losses have stunned the Crimson Tide, but the Tigers are the only ranked team left. The Iron Bowl could be attractive if Auburn keeps it up and serves as the spoiler during rivalry weekend.

The Bruins just keep winning. Many -- including myself -- thought the Bruins could lose to Wisconsin on Saturday after losing Nico Iamaleava for the season and the Badgers coming off a bye, but it didn't happen. The best-case scenario for UCLA, aside from a 13-0 regular season capped by a Big Ten title, would be to suffer a late loss and watch two others play on championship weekend so it can begin CFP prep. Just don't tell Chesney that.
Projection: (10) Kentucky at (7) Ole Miss

Could the SEC get a fifth team in? It may come down to a 10-win team from another Power Four vs. a three-loss SEC squad with potentially multiple ranked victories. Why not Will Stein and Kentucky? This team is rolling right now. We're not necessarily projecting three losses for the Wildcats. They're 6-1 right now and still very much in the SEC Championship conversation.

Has Pete Golding and the Ole Miss defense finally figured it out? The Rebels' 28-point victory over Missouri was notable because Ole Miss dominated at the line of scrimmage for the first time this season against a top-tier opponent. That means something moving forward with Texas, Georgia, Oklahoma and Mississippi State still left to play for the one-loss Rebels. Ole Miss misses Kentucky during the regular season.
Projection: (11) Notre Dame at (6) Tennessee

The last-team-in designation this season is going to be hotly debated in the hours leading up to the CFP's final reveal. Could a one-loss Texas Tech be skipped over in favor of Notre Dame? Watching the Fighting Irish get pushed around by BYU in Provo for much of the contest wasn't on the bingo card, but championship-level teams play their best when pressed into a corner, and Notre Dame has one final chance to deliver against Miami later this year. This is not a team we've projected to go unbeaten at any point this fall, by the way. Now, Notre Dame must beat the Hurricanes in November . If not, 10-2 is where things get tricky.

Tennessee has two ranked opponents left after a momentum-seizing victory over Alabama. That's about as favorable a slate you could want down the stretch in a conference beating itself up every weekend this season. At worst, the Vols need to split their remaining matchups with Kentucky and LSU and reach 10 wins. Next weekend's tussle at South Carolina will likely nuke CFP hopes with a loss, unless Tennessee goes unbeaten in November.
Projection: (12) Oregon State (5) Indiana

Week 7 in college football was crazy enough, so why not toss the Beavers in as the 12-seed this week with an 11-win, Pac-12 champion projection dictated by all-everything wideout Jesse Legree? There's not a team playing more complete football than Oregon State since Week 3, on the heels of five straight blowout victories. The dilemma here is JMU and where the Dukes land. If they're 13-0, it's unlikely the selection committee would put a two-loss Group of Six team ahead of Napier's unblemished group.

We're projecting the Hoosiers to finish as the Big Ten's runner-up this season at 11-2 overall, without being docked for losing in the conference title game. That would slot Indiana somewhere in the 6-8 range and guarantee a first-round home game. For the defending national champions, seeding no longer matters after their 22-game winning streak was snapped against Ohio State. Getting to the CFP is the top priority from here.
Quarterfinals
PEACH BOWL — Projection: (9) Alabama vs. (1) Miami

The Hurricanes had won five straight games at home by at least 28 points prior to Saturday night's letdown, one that tosses a wrench in the ACC title conversation and this playoff bracket. They're not going to look flawless every week and have a lot to fix after that one. We're downgrading Miami, but keeping the Hurricanes in the No. 1 spot for now, considering all the other elites that lost on Saturday.

Give the Seminoles credit for not giving up under Mike Norvell despite obvious distractions his regime faces at midseason. For Miami, staying healthy before the battle at Notre Dame is the goal. I thought we were finished worrying about ? That was a close one.

ROSE BOWL — Projection: (6) Tennessee vs. (3) Ohio State

There's reason to worry if you're a Buckeyes fan following Julian Sayin's throwing arm injury suffered at Indiana. It was a game Ohio State absolutely needed to win, but the prognosis for when the quarterback will return is unclear. Ryan Day after the game. Could this be fatal for the Buckeyes with USC, Oregon, Northwestern and Nebraska looming? Yes, but this team has the talent to lean on its defense for a few games until Sayin returns. That doesn't mean they're going to go unbeaten for the remainder and get to the Big Ten title game, though.

articles.headline: Deadly fire breaks out at Canada military base
keyFacts: A large fire at the Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta caused casualties, defence minister David McGuinty said.
The blaze spread rapidly due to high winds and the cause is currently being investigated by authorities.
Local authorities urged residents to avoid the area while neighbouring provinces offered emergency resources and support.
body: - Published
A large fire near a Canadian military base in Alberta has killed and injured some people, the defence minister said, without confirming the number of casualties.

The Canadian Armed Forces were working with local authorities to manage the fire and were looking into what caused it, David McGuinty said, describing the situation as "very, very active and delicate".
Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney said on X that a "serious incident creating a major fire" had occurred, adding his "thoughts are with all the brave women and men affected".
Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, where the fire broke out, is one of the country's busiest military training bases.

The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation describes it as "the principal base for live fire training exercises". About 690 military personnel and 300 civilian workers are on site on a regular day, according to the CBC.
Saturday's blaze "spread rapidly due to high winds" and had torn through the fences of the base, the Municipal District of Wainwright said.
McGuinty told reporters he "cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory".

Alberta's premier Danielle Smith says the "significant and tragic fire" is "affecting many of [the province's] brave military personnel". Provincial authorities are in touch with the central government in managing and investigating the situation, she added.
It is unclear when the fire broke out, but the district first posted about the incident at about 17:30 local time (23:30 GMT).
Local authorities have urged residents to avoid the area and give all emergency vehicles right of way.
Neighbouring provinces have offered their support.

Saskatchewan premier Scott Moe says he has deployed resources to Alberta and is "ready to provide more if required", while British Columbia premier David Eby says his government has "reached out to Alberta to offer all possible assistance".

articles.headline: Every Major Game Releasing in November That Isn’t GTA 6
keyFacts: Polygon reported that many developers moved their games out of November to avoid competing with Grand Theft Auto 6.
Polygon stated that several alternative games are releasing in November, including Gravhounds, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered, and World of Warcraft: Forever.
Polygon noted that other November releases feature titles like The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Barbie Rewind, and Milki Delivery.
body: For millions of gamers, November is all about one video game: Grand Theft Auto 6. Rockstar’s much-anticipated open-world crime game is likely to spark a cultural moment that we haven’t seen in games since Animal Crossing: New Horizons in 2020. While that’s exciting, it’s also bound to leave players who don’t care about GTA a little bored considering that so many developers have moved their games out of November entirely to avoid getting lost in the storm.

The good news for anyone looking for some good GTA 6 counter-programming is that there are more games coming out next month. While it’s not as crowded a field as we typically get in November, there’s still sure to be something for you. Here’s a look at some of the highlights you can expect to play if you’re avoiding the streets of Vice City.
Gravhounds
Release date: Nov. 2
Where to play: Windows PC, Xbox Series X

In a crowded Gamescom Opening Night Live stream, Gravhounds was a real attention-grabber. The upcoming co-op shooter puts you and your friends in control of gun-toting dogs forced to shoot their way through an alien planet. With base building mechanics and some gravity-bending physics to toy with, it could wind up being a goofy multiplayer hit. It’s set to launch into early access starting on Nov. 2.
Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered
Release date: Nov. 3
Where to play: Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox Series X

Anyone who grew up in the GameCube era will no doubt remember Godzilla: Destroy All Monster Melee, if only for its iconic cover art. 24 years after its release, the cult classic kaiju brawler is returning in a freshly remastered form complete with online multiplayer. If you’ve never played it, don’t sleep on it: It’s a surprisingly fun casual fighting game that’s filled with classic monsters.
World of Warcraft: Forever
Release date: Nov. 4
Where to play: Windows PC

Arguably, World of Warcraft: Forever is as big a deal as GTA 6 — at least for a specific era of players. Blizzard is embracing 2000s nostalgia by creating an all-new version of its legendary MMO that features retro graphics and brand-new content. It’s a dream come true for players who have just always wanted more from World of Warcraft, but as they remember it back in its heyday.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
Release date: Nov. 5
Where to play: Nintendo Switch 2

Considering that GTA 6 isn’t coming to Switch 2, we always knew that Nintendo would need to pull out the big guns to counter-program it. It doesn’t get much bigger than a remake of the greatest game of all time. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is getting a modern makeover complete with dreamy visuals, modernized controls, and even a jump button.
Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School
Release date: Nov. 5
Where to play: PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox Series X

For those looking for a multiplayer game to play in lieu of GTA 6 missing an opportunity for co-op, Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School is your best bet. The multiplayer puzzle game will drop you and a pal into a series of escape rooms designed by people who used to make them in real life. It even features local split screen, making it a perfect couples game for Jason and Lucia.
Warhammer Survivors
Release date: Nov. 10
Where to play: Android, iOS, Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox Series X

Sometimes a game title says it all. Warhammer Survivors is Vampire Survivors, but Warhammer. It’s made by the developers behind the excellent Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun, a studio that has already proven that it knows how to work Warhammer lore into a good retro genre game.
Barbie Rewind
Release date: Nov. 12
Where to play: Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox Series X

Barbie Rewind might be the smartest bit of counter-programming you’ll find in November. While GTA 6 is catering to those who crave a hyper-violent crime simulator, this good-natured retro collection pulls together tons of beloved Barbie games released between 1991 and 2007. If you grew up playing games like Barbie: Super Model, this may very well be your GTA 6.
Sonic Pico Park
Release date: Nov. 12
Where to play: Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, Windows PC

Even Sonic the Hedgehog isn’t scared of GTA 6. Sega will celebrate the Blue Blur’s 35th anniversary this year with Sonic Pico Park, a Sonic-themed spin-off of the multiplayer Pico Park series. Expect a 2D puzzle platformer that gives you a lot of reasons to curse your friends as you work together to solve co-op puzzles.
Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy
Release date: Nov. 12
Where to play: Nintendo Switch 2

Pikmin 4 is the latest Switch game to get the full Switch 2 Edition treatment, and it’s a great choice. The strategy game is one of the Switch’s best thanks to its satisfying critter-commanding and feel-good vibe. The updated version comes with Dandori Academy, a stage-structured challenge mode that’s meant to test your organization skills.
Milki Delivery
Release date: Nov. 17
Where to play: Windows PC

If you’re more of a cozy gamer, Milki Delivery should be on your radar. The 2D indie charmer puts you in charge of a dairy delivery service. You’ll bike around the scenic countryside delivering milk straight from your cows to the locals. It all has the inviting vibes of a Studio Ghibli film.

articles.headline: Vance says he’ll ‘have to make a decision’ on 2028 presidential run after midterm elections
keyFacts: Vice President JD Vance stated during a town hall that he will have to decide on a 2028 presidential run after the midterm elections.
Vance cited his four young children and his wife's reluctance regarding politics as factors when considering his future political decisions.
Vance is among several potential 2028 contenders from both political parties mentioned in discussions about the upcoming presidential cycle.
body: Vice President JD Vance addressed widespread speculation he will run for president in the 2028 election cycle during a town hall released on Saturday night.

While speaking with Tony Dokoupil of CBS News in Michigan, Vance was asked whether there’s a chance he won’t run for president in 2028. He has long been floated as a likely heir to President Donald Trump’s political life alongside Secretary of State Marco Rubio, though neither has publicly committed to running.

“Of course there’s a chance,” he said. “Yeah, man, we’ve got four little kids. My wife has never loved politics, she loves public service. I think you can do a lot of good in this job, and I’ve tried to do as much good as possible. But, I really, people ask me this question all the time, and I think they assume because I’m a politician, ‘of course he’s going to run for president in 2028.’ The way that I think about big life decisions, my wife will tell you this, is I’m a procrastinator. I hate thinking about it. And what will happen is, that, first of all, after all these fine people elect Mike Rogers United States Senator for the state of Michigan, what’s going to happen is then I’ll have to think about. And then I will actually have to make a decision. But, you know, anything can happen, man, anything.”

Vance’s name is on a lengthy list of potential 2028 contenders, including Democrats such as Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY), Gov. Gavin Newsom (D-CA), and former Vice President Kamala Harris . Vance would likely benefit from having served as the executive branch’s second-ranking official for four years if he runs, but would be inherently tied to Trump’s waning popularity and to how his exit from office toward the end of the decade plays out.
WHERE THE TOP 2028 CONTENDERS ARE HEADING AHEAD OF THE MIDTERM ELECTIONS

The town hall was held in Monroe, a small city near Detroit. Vance also fielded questions about data center development, allegations of corruption within the White House, and high domestic gas prices, both from Dokoupil and members of the audience.

“I fundamentally trust the judgment of the American people,” he said when asked if he believes Republicans will retain control of the Senate in November’s midterm elections . He also acknowledged the conflict in Iran’s impact on domestic energy prices, saying, “I will be the first one to tell you gas prices are too high,” but that “in some ways, we have won decisively.” He also said the United States’s military has destroyed the “Iranian nuclear program,” and the White House is now working toward securing a deal that ensures Iran doesn’t rebuild their nuclear arsenal and finding a long-term solution to disrupt shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.headline: Rays punish Cleveland defensive lapses to square ALCS at two games apiece
keyFacts: The Tampa Bay Rays defeated the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 on Saturday to tie the AL Championship Series at two games apiece.
Jonathan Aranda drove in two runs in the seventh inning following a defensive error by right fielder Chase DeLauter.
Game 5 of the series is scheduled for Sunday in Cleveland.
body: Jonathan Aranda’s single led to two runs in the seventh inning when the ball got by right fielder Chase DeLauter, Nick Martinez pitched five and one-third innings for his first postseason win and the Tampa Bay Rays defeated the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 on Saturday night to even the AL Championship Series at 2-2.

Game 5 of the best-of-seven matchup is Sunday in Cleveland before the series shifts back to St Petersburg, Florida, on Monday. There is no off day for travel after Friday’s game was postponed by rain.
Cleveland’s Travis Bazzana hit his first postseason home run but also committed a fielding error at second base on a tough night for the Guardians’ defense.

The first four hitters in the Rays’ order – Yandy Díaz, Aranda, Chandler Simpson and Junior Caminero – had six of the Rays’ 11 hits and drove in six runs after going seven for 41 with three RBIs in the first three ALCS games.

Aranda had three hits and drove in two runs after going hitless in 10 at-bats in the first three games. Díaz had two hits and two RBIs, including a two-run homer in the ninth off Matt Festa, while Simpson and Caminero each drove in a run.

Pitching on a 46-degree night, Martinez (1-0) allowed one run and two hits in his second career postseason start and 10th appearance. After DeLauter’s RBI single put Cleveland ahead 1-0 in the first, Martinez retired 10 consecutive batters at one point before walking Bazzana to lead off the fifth.
Tampa Bay took a 2-1 lead in the sixth when Caminero lined a double to the left-field wall off Daniel Espino (0-1), then broke open the game with a three-run seventh.

Richie Palacios and Taylor Walls reached on base hits and moved into scoring position on a double steal. After Díaz struck out, Aranda lined a single past a diving Bazzana, who was playing near the grass between first and second, and into right field. Palacios scored, and when DeLauter allowed the ball to get under his glove, Walls came around from second. Aranda went all the way to third and scored on Simpson’s sacrifice fly.
Bazzana homered in the seventh against Ian Seymour and Brayan Rocchio added an RBI single as Cleveland closed to 5-3.
Shawn Armstrong opened and struck out one batter in the first inning before giving way to Foster Griffin.

articles.headline: Fire breaks out after deadly incident at Canadian military base, officials say
keyFacts: Defense Minister David McGuinty said people were killed and injured in an incident at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright that caused a major fire.
McGuinty stated that the Royal Canadian Mounted Police are investigating the active and delicate situation while authorities coordinate the emergency response.
McGuinty said authorities were still working to determine what happened and expected to provide further information.
body: Canada's defense minister said Saturday that people were killed and injured in an incident at a military base in Alberta that caused a major fire.
"I'm saddened to share that there have been both fatalities and injuries as a result of an incident on the base," Defense Minister David McGuinty said.
The incident occurred at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, located about 112 miles southeast of Edmonton.

"We are dealing with a serious incident at CFB Wainwright, and are fully engaged with federal, provincial and local authorities," said Gen. Jennie Carignan, chief of the defense staff for the Canadian Armed Forces, in a social media post. "Our priority remains the welfare of our members, their families and their community, and my thoughts are with all those affected by this incident."

McGuinty did not provide casualty figures or details about what caused the incident. He said the Royal Canadian Mounted Police were involved in the investigation and described the situation as "very, very active and delicate."

The Canadian Armed Forces and federal, provincial and local authorities were coordinating the emergency response, he said. The nearby community of Wainwright was providing hospital and firefighting support.

The Municipal District of Wainwright said the fire crossed the base's fence earlier Saturday and was spreading rapidly due to high winds. Firefighters from multiple jurisdictions were responding, and no evacuation order was in effect.
"Our thoughts are with all the brave women and men affected," Prime Minister Mark Carney said earlier in a social media post.
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith described the fire as "significant and tragic" and said it was affecting many military personnel.

Canadian Forces Base Wainwright is one of Canada's busiest military training bases, where soldiers prepare for combat operations. It is home to the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, which conducts realistic battlefield exercises, and the 3rd Canadian Division Training Centre, which provides military training.
McGuinty said authorities were still working to determine what happened and expected to provide further information.
Carney said the federal government was working closely with Alberta officials and local authorities. He said he and Smith were in close contact, as were their ministers and officials.
Smith thanked first responders and those providing care and support to those affected.
Canadian Conservative opposition leader Pierre Poilievre said he had spoken with Carney and the defense minister to offer support to those affected by the fire.
"Pray for Wainwright, everyone," Poilievre said in a social media post. He urged people in the area to follow emergency instructions and keep roads clear for first responders.
Neither Carney nor Smith provided details about what caused the fire or whether anyone was injured.
The fire came days before the province is set to vote on beginning a process that could lead to its seeking independence from Canada.

articles.headline: Stephen A. Smith recounts four-hour White House dinner with Trump and Bill Maher: ‘Wouldn’t let us leave’
keyFacts: Commentator Stephen A. Smith and comedian Bill Maher attended a four-hour dinner at the White House with President Donald Trump on Thursday night.
Smith stated that Trump answered every question and remained defiant against criticism during the substantive and respectful meeting.
The group discussed various topics including the economy, the conflict in Iran, and Historically Black Colleges.
body: Sports pundit and political commentator Stephen A. Smith recounted what he said was a four-hour dinner with comedian Bill Maher and President Donald Trump , hosted at the White House on Thursday night.

“Essentially, it amounted to what I consider to be a very substantive evening,” Smith said. “We were there for over four hours in the White House. And Donald Trump did not run from any question. He answered every single question. He was very, very defiant with any criticism that came in his direction or any disagreement. But as Kid Rock went on Fox News on Friday morning and articulated, it was a pleasant meeting. It was respectful.”

Smith was invited to the dinner by Maher, who had attended a dinner at the White House with Trump in March 2025, an event notable largely for Maher’s subsequent address about the evening, which was described as friendly rather than adversarial despite the pair’s history of publicly attacking each other. Smith similarly said he enjoyed the meeting and appreciated Trump’s willingness to speak with figures with whom he disagrees.

“I don’t consider myself a liberal, I don’t consider myself a conservative, I’m a registered independent,” Smith said of his political affiliation. “I say that all the time.” Smith, who has broadly functioned as a left-wing figure throughout his career, has increasingly interviewed Republican figures on his own show since Trump won the 2024 presidential election and has at times split with Democrats on certain issues. Smith has been floated as a potential celebrity 2028 presidential candidate, not too unlike Trump himself, though the radio host shot down such rumors for fear of being “taken off the air.”

“The dinner last night… was great, I think they had a good time,” Trump said of the meeting. “We talked about everything. It lasted a long time. And you know, even though they have to sort of, you know, put on a sort of facade for their people, they like Trump. And I actually like them. We had a great time. We even took a little tour of the ballroom.”

“It was a great dinner. It was a very informative dinner. Smart people. Stephen A. is great, Bill Maher, I tell you what, he likes me a lot more than people understand. And I actually like him.” Trump had gone after Smith in a rant over the summer, calling him an “arrogant fool” and “dumb as a rock” over a disagreement stemming from Trump’s attendance at an NBA Finals game the New York Knicks lost.
STEPHEN A. SMITH REJECTS 2028 RUN FOR FEAR OF BEING ‘TAKEN OFF THE AIR’

“He deserves to be recognized for his hospitality and his unwillingness to run from any single issue we brought up that he disagreed with,” Smith also said, despite his history of criticizing the president. “When I say we were there for over four hours, it was because of him. He wouldn’t let us leave. And we were bringing up stuff, trying to pummel him with it. He wouldn’t bend.” The group discussed the economy, the conflict in Iran, Texas Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton, and Trump’s White House projects.

Trump and Smith have known each other since long before Trump first ran for president, and Smith often recounts Trump calling him about his desire to purchase the Buffalo Bills in 2014. Smith said much of his motivation for attending the meeting was to discuss the Trump administration’s approach to policies regarding Historically Black Colleges.

articles.headline: Michigan Democrat confirms sister-in-law's terror watchlist lawsuit days before Obama campaign appearance
keyFacts: Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed confirmed Saturday that his sister-in-law was a plaintiff in a 2016 lawsuit over the federal terrorist watchlist.

body: Michigan Democrat Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed acknowledged Saturday night that his sister-in-law was involved in a federal terrorist watchlist lawsuit during the Obama administration, just days before former President Barack Obama is scheduled to campaign alongside him.

El-Sayed was confronted by Fox News senior correspondent Mike Tobin about court documents identifying his sister-in-law, Mariam Jukaku, as a plaintiff in a 2016 lawsuit challenging her alleged placement on the federal Terrorism Screening Database , commonly known as the terrorist watchlist.
"There's reporting in a lawsuit that now backs it up. And documentation with the lawsuit that Mariam Jukaku, who's your sister-in-law, that she was on the terrorist watch list?" Tobin asked.
"Yeah," El-Sayed responded.

El-Sayed then defended his sister-in-law, insisting she had committed no wrongdoing and turning his criticism toward Republican Senate rival Mike Rogers.

"She did nothing wrong and was captured on that and then sued and got off," El-Sayed said. "You've got this system where folks are guilty until proven innocent because they've got different kinds of names, because of the infrastructure that people like Mike Rogers set up."
The exchange comes as Obama prepares to campaign alongside El-Sayed in Michigan on Oct. 24, ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm election .

body: Democrats are running up lopsided majorities of the early votes as Americans head to the polls and mail in their ballots, carving out a clear majority of the votes cast so far.
Of early and mail-in voters, 54% were Democrats, 30% Republicans and 16% independents or “other,” according to state election data compiled by TargetSmart and NBC News.
The early vote advantage carries over to the marquee Senate races, including several held in Republican-leaning states.
In Michigan, where Democrat Abdul El-Sayed is battling former Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.), the Democratic edge is 55-36%, based on voters’ registrations.
In Iowa, where Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-Iowa) is in a tough race with Democrat Josh Turek, the edge from registered Democrats is 57-29%, with 14% from “other.”
None of the data show how people actually voted – just who showed up or sent in their ballot.
“We know the Democrats have the enthusiasm advantage,” said University of Kentucky political scientist Stephen Voss.
But what remains to be seen is whether the early numbers point to a predicted overall wave of voters or merely “upper status voters who always vote anyway,” he added.
One way to explore that is to compare numbers to four years ago.

In Republican-leaning Nebraska, where Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts is battling independent Dan Osborne, the Democratic edge has expanded from then. It’s 45-38 now, compared to 44-41 at this point in voting in 2022.
Eighty-nine percent of Democrats who have voted in Nebraska also voted in 2022 and 2024, while 10% are new voters, according to the secretary of state.
For Republicans, 91% voted in the past but just 7% are new voters.
Virginia is seeing a flood of early turnout, with 519,000 ballots in compared to 260,000 by this point in 2022, with the total doubling in left-leaning Fairfax County.
In Texas, the which features a high-profile race between Democratic state Rep. James Talarico (D-Texas) and AG Ken Paxton (R-Texas), Democratic edge is an overwhelming 62-32%.
Democrats historically tend to vote early or by mail, although President Trump has regularly blasted mail-voting in favor of in-person voting on Election Day, calling it “inherently corrupt.”
But this year, on campaign stops and online, he has been changing his message.

In a video last weekend, Trump told supporters from the Oval Office: “If your state has early voting, do not wait. Go out and vote. Vote early, vote by mail, or vote in person on Election Day, November 3rd, so we can defeat the radical left ‘Dumocrats’ in a midterm victory that is too big to rig.”
He also told voters to “pretend I’m on the ballot.”

articles.headline: Trump Faults Aides As Republican Midterm Prospects Dim
keyFacts: Trump is not on the November 3 ballot but repeatedly tells supporters to pretend that he is, hoping to mobilize voters who might otherwise skip the election.

He has embarked on a frenetic campaign schedule while largely avoiding acknowledging his own role in shaping the strategy and how his unpopularity is weighing on Republican candidates in competitive races.
Much of the friction has centered on James Blair, the longtime aide who runs Trump’s super PAC MAGA Inc., and White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, who until now had largely escaped criticism.
body: WASHINGTON, Oct 17 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump is blaming senior aides and political operatives for a faltering midterm strategy, questioning campaign spending, faulting redistricting and second-guessing candidate choices as Republicans fight to retain control of Congress, said three people familiar with internal discussions.

Trump is not on the November 3 ballot but repeatedly tells supporters to pretend that he is, hoping to mobilize voters who might otherwise skip the election. He has embarked on a frenetic campaign schedule while largely avoiding acknowledging his own role in shaping the strategy and how his unpopularity is weighing on Republican candidates in competitive races.

Much of the friction has centered on James Blair, the longtime aide who runs Trump’s super PAC MAGA Inc., and White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, who until now had largely escaped criticism. Trump has faulted Blair’s handling of campaign funds, while some White House officials and allies have questioned Wiles’ oversight of the political operation.

As Trump questions why campaign spending has failed to improve Republican polling numbers, his advisers are also blaming one another. Wiles has pointed to Blair, while Blair has faulted the White House legislative affairs team, one of the people said.
“What’s really happening is a circular firing squad,” the person said.

Opinion polls suggest Democrats will win the House of Representatives, while the Senate remains too close to call. Losing the House would hamper Trump’s legislative agenda in the final two years of his term and give Democrats subpoena power to investigate his administration.
Trump defended Wiles on Friday, calling her “smart” and “tough” and saying she would remain in her job. “Susie is here, and she’s going to be here for a long time,” he said.
White House spokesman Davis Ingle rejected the sources’ characterization, saying they were “armchair experts peddling their baseless speculation.” Wiles did not respond to a request for comment.
Trump Has Long Distanced Himself From Political Setbacks

Trump has long sought to distance himself from political setbacks. He refused to accept his defeat in the 2020 election and said ahead of the 2022 midterm results that he deserved “all the credit” if Republicans won but “should not be blamed at all” if they lost. More recently, he has reminded audiences that the president’s party typically struggles in midterm elections.

But Trump helped devise and drive some of the strategies he is now questioning, including the redistricting effort and candidate choices shaped by his personal loyalties or grievances. His approval rating is at the lowest point of his presidency, weighed down by voter concern over high prices and dissatisfaction with the Iran war.

Trump’s frustrations with his political team spilled into public view after Blair and Chris LaCivita, who co-managed Trump’s 2024 campaign, traveled in early October to Republika Srpska, a self-governing region of Bosnia. The New York Times reported the men received substantial payments to advise the regional government ahead of local elections.

Trump distanced himself from both men, describing them as “outside consultants” in an October 7 Truth Social post and warning that if he found a conflict of interest, he would “terminate them, immediately!”
Senior White House officials questioned why Blair was taking on lucrative work overseas when he was supposed to be overseeing the final stretch of the Republican campaign, three people said.
One person said Wiles approved the trip without informing Trump, raising questions about how closely she was overseeing his political advisers.
For Trump, the larger concern is that Blair’s outside work has distracted him from his political responsibilities, two people said.

In a statement, Blair said: “All of this mudslinging is ridiculous, and counterproductive. President Trump and me are focused on helping Republicans win in November. Every other Republican should be doing the same.”

In a separate statement, LaCivita said: “President Trump and his team are and always have been focused on the midterms. That’s demonstrated through the money, message and motivation that the president is bringing on the road and all year. Sniping from unnamed cowards who’ve never been in a fight is not worth responding to.”
$200 Million And Redistricting

With Trump asking why Republican polling in pivotal races has not improved despite MAGA Inc.’s campaign spending, which public records put at $200 million so far, it remains unclear whether he will approve more spending before the election, one of the sources said.

Trump also has pressed political aides and advisers in the past week to explain why the redistricting effort he personally pushed has failed to deliver more clear-cut Republican gains, two sources said.

Texas is a particular concern. Republicans redrew the state’s congressional map to gain seats, but the strategy relies in part on Hispanic voters turning out as they did for the 2024 election. Opinion polls suggest that support may be difficult to replicate amid concerns about the cost of living and Trump’s handling of the economy. Some Republicans fear the new boundaries could backfire, leaving incumbents more vulnerable instead of giving the party an advantage.
“The redistricting diced up the Trump voters too much,” one of the sources said.

Trump had said Blair was expected to return to the White House after the midterms, describing his departure as a “short leave of absence.” But two sources said his return was now unlikely. “He’s not coming back. That is not happening,” one of them said.

It was less clear how things would play out for Wiles, who played a central role in Trump’s 2024 victory and has been credited by Trump allies and aides with bringing greater discipline to his White House in his second term.
Trump “may be annoyed at certain things but she has effectively kept that machine going,” a fourth source close to the White House said.

articles.headline: You don't have to turn off your phone to switch SIM cards (but you probably should)
keyFacts: Most modern smartphones allow users to switch physical SIM cards while the device remains powered on.
Powering down the phone or enabling airplane mode before swapping can prevent minor software-related network errors.
Users with shared SIM and microSD trays must unmount their microSD card first to prevent data loss.
body: You don't have to turn off your phone to switch SIM cards (but you probably should)
A quick step removes the small chance of anything going wrong and requiring more of your time.

If your phone has a SIM tray, it's not something you likely open often, but there are still reasons to. You may be switching to an MVNO to save money, or maybe you're temporarily swapping out your normal SIM for a cheaper local carrier when travelling. In some cases, your carrier will send you a replacement card if yours is damaged.

Most of today's smartphones let you switch SIMs with the phone on, so you don't need to switch your device off for the process. But there are modest benefits if you do, and for something so quick, it's better to be safe if you have a few minutes.
How to replace the SIM

We're talking about physical SIM cards, which you have to remove from your phone by hand. eSIM replacement should be as simple as using a QR code, carrier app or direct transfer between different smartphones. Most eSIM-compatible phones can store many eSIMS, though only a few can be active at once.
Physical SIM card replacement involves these steps:
- Optionally, power down your phone or enable airplane mode.
- Pop the tray out, usually by gently pushing a paperclip or SIM ejector tool into the ejection pinhole on the phone.
- Change the card, ensuring you use the correct card size.
- Pop the tray back into place.
- Enter your PIN or restart if the phone requests it.
If you have a dual-SIM phone that supports two physical cards, check which SIM you intend to swap before you begin.

While many argue eSIM is a superior technology because it requires no moving parts, others still appreciate the convenience and relative privacy true SIM cards provide. They make it easy to install and use over-the-counter pay-as-you-go SIM-based accounts, for example.
The small potential risks of SIM replacement

Most potential dangers of SIM replacement are physical. You might accidentally insert dirt, grime or moisture into the SIM tray, or force a larger card into a smaller slot incorrectly. You could also break the SIM tray so it no longer aligns correctly, or otherwise harm the card. A damaged SIM card or one incorrectly inserted may cause the phone to continue trying (and failing) to create a network connection, draining its battery and causing it to overheat.

Most people never encounter these problems, since slowing down and being careful does the trick. In most cases, your phone will take a moment to read the new SIM and find the network. Then it will be available for service, subject to account setup requirements.

The benefit of turning your phone off before swapping the SIM is minor. It forces your phone to look at the fresh information provided on the new card when it powers on again, helping register your device on its new network more quickly by reading the new carrier settings. This reduces the chance you'll encounter a software-based "network error" message when you swap.
More to think about when swapping SIMs

Before the 2010s, SIM slots were usually located underneath a phone's removable battery, which obviously required powering off the device to access. Over time, as removable batteries became less common, SIM trays were moved to the outside of phones. Early models using this setup would often show a network error if you swapped SIMs while the phone was on, but they quickly became hot-swappable and this was no longer a problem.

You don't even need to switch your device off completely to make the phone refresh its carrier settings from the card. You'll get a similar result if you turn on airplane mode, wait 30 seconds before swapping the SIM and turn airplane mode off again once the new SIM is inserted. This should prevent any carrier hiccups during the process.
A warning on SD cards

Unlike the iPhone, some Android devices still include a microSD card slot. In some cases, this is in the same tray as the SIM, though placement varies. If this is the case for you, as when ejecting an external drive, it's important to unmount the microSD card before removing the SIM to prevent losing data. On Samsung devices: open the My Files app, find the SD Card, tap the three-dot menu next to it and choose Unmount. Search the Settings app or check online documentation if you're not sure how this works for your device.

So while the benefits are slight, switching off your phone when replacing the SIM can prevent software-related glitches. If you don't want to power down, use airplane mode instead. And in case you encounter a network error after swapping, always try restarting your device first.

articles.headline: Arizona joins Nevada to fight proposed cuts to their shares of Colorado River
keyFacts: Arizona joined Nevada in a legal battle against the Trump administration over proposed cuts to their shares of the Colorado River.
The interior department announced restrictions that could slash water supplied to lower basin states due to historically low reservoir levels.
Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs stated the legal action is necessary because the federal government refuses to hold the upper basin accountable.
body: Arizona has joined Nevada in its legal battle against the Trump administration’s proposed cuts to their shares of the shrinking Colorado River.

The move comes after the interior department announced restrictions this summer that could slash the water supplied to lower basin states – Arizona, California and Nevada – over the next two years depending on the river’s condition.
The river’s major reservoirs, Lake Mead and Lake Powell, have plummeted to historically low levels, due to overuse and a changing climate.

The states sharing the waterway were at an impasse with the upper basin states arguing that their downstream counterparts were responsible for the reservoir’s water shortages and should thus face the largest cuts.
The federal government’s intervention came after the states missed several deadlines for a consensus.
The fear looming over the state of the river is that if reservoir levels plunged far enough, the waterway would effectively not be able to flow downstream, a so-called deadpool.
The upper basin states – Wyoming, Colorado, Utah and New Mexico – were spared from the water cuts, an exemption that has drawn sharp rebuke from the leaders of the lower basin states.
“We are drawing a line in the sand,” Arizona governor Katie Hobbs said in a Friday statement.

“I am taking this legal action alongside Nevada because the federal government refuses to hold the Upper Basin accountable for the water deliveries they owe Arizona, and is threatening to force draconian cuts that go well beyond the Lower Basin Agreement,” Hobbs continued, referring to a two-year-voluntary water conservation pact among her state, California and Nevada.

Tom Buschatzke, the director of Arizona’s water department, said “intervention in the Nevada lawsuit is necessary at this time for Arizona to protect its legal rights to Colorado River water while preserving a path forward to achieving a collaborative outcome with California and Nevada to protect the Colorado River system”.
An interior department spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the joint litigation.

Sunday 18 October 2026 01:06, UK

articles.headline: Dev Behind Russian Roulette Drinking Game Cancels Steam Demo Plans Following AI Copycat Concerns
keyFacts: Alliance Arts canceled the public Steam demo for the game Drunken Goddess Reflux over concerns about potential AI-generated copycats.
The developers said that releasing a public demo could allow others to quickly produce imitating works using AI tools ahead of the game's launch.
Alliance Arts will replace the public demo with a closed online play session and the full game remains scheduled for a December 8, 2026 release.
body: The developer behind Russian roulette anime game Drunken Goddess Reflux has canceled its plans for a public Steam demo, citing concerns over potential AI copycats.

Alliance Arts and Who You's path to launch has seemingly been mostly bump-free since it was announced back in April. Featuring ghostly pinks and purples and a gameplay premise described as "shot glass Russian roulette with a demon who loves you enough to kill you," the recent reveal that it would launch this December only made its future feel clearer.

Part of that release date announcement included the promise that a demo would launch October 19, but as explained in an update post on Steam , those plans have changed. What was originally intended to be a public release for the Drunken Goddess Reflux demo has now been canceled in favor of a "closed play session for a limited number of participants." It's a last-minute move Alliance Arts apologized for, but its concerns related to rapidly advancing AI technology were simply too great to ignore.

"We are concerned that, based on the content of the demo, works imitating or replicating this game's presentation and gameplay could be quickly produced using AI or other tools and released ahead of the game's launch," the developers said in their list of concerns.

In other words, sending a demo out into the wild could open the door for nefarious individuals to use AI to generate a low-effort clone or copycat experience. For a team hoping for a successful launch in just a few months, someone coming in to steal its thunder could potentially throw a wrench into things.

Alliance Arts' fears emerge amid a time when AI is seeping into the gaming industry in ways most may not have ever expected. For example, mods – including mashups of Elden Ring and Super Mario 64 or Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 and Skate – have regularly gone viral on social media in recent weeks. With the controversial technology expanding in new, unforeseen ways every day, it's a risk the Drunken Goddess Reflux weren't willing to take.

Another bullet point concern listed in its message detailed restrictions on posting and streaming gameplay videos, but as the team explained, they "are not currently in a position to properly handle and manage those restrictions." With limited resources to keep nearly unrestricted access to a demo in check, Alliance Arts is moving forward with that closed demo.

"We will therefore hold online play sessions in a closed environment," the developer added, "open to those who have reviewed and agreed in advance to the participation requirements and the rules on posting and streaming gameplay videos."

Players interested in trying the demonic drinking game out were encouraged to join the Discord server presented in the Steam post. Otherwise, Drunken Goddess Reflux is still scheduled to launch on PC via Steam December 8, 2026.

articles.headline: Dubois destroys Wardley in two rounds to retain title
keyFacts: Daniel Dubois defeated Fabio Wardley by a second-round stoppage to retain his WBO heavyweight title in London.
Dubois floored Wardley with a straight right in the first round before overwhelming him with punches in the second round, prompting Wardley's corner to throw in the towel.
The victory extended Dubois' professional record to 24 wins and marked his second successive stoppage victory over Wardley.
body: - Published
Daniel Dubois underlined his status as Britain's leading heavyweight with a devastating second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley to retain his WBO title in London.
The 29-year-old floored Wardley with a straight right inside the opening 20 seconds of their eagerly anticipated rematch at the O2 Arena and continued his relentless assault.
Wardley survived the opening round but was overwhelmed by another sustained attack in the second, prompting his corner to throw in the towel.
Dubois registers a second successive stoppage victory over Wardley, just five months after climbing off the canvas twice to dethrone his British rival in a thrilling 11-round contest in Manchester.
This time, there was no such drama for the champion, who was dominant from the opening bell as he extended his professional record to 24 wins - 23 by knockout - and three defeats.
"Fabio is a great boy, coming in for the second time, but it was my time and my era. I had my intentions, bad intentions from the beginning," Dubois said.
"My back was against the wall the first time, this time we just had to go out there and show that we mean business, which is what we did tonight."
Wardley, 31, suffered the second defeat of his 23-fight professional career.
Dubois comes out with intent in one-sided title defence
A sell-out crowd of 19,000 packed the O2 Arena and made their allegiances clear.

Wardley's charismatic yet measured personality has made him a popular figure. He looked full of purpose as he took his time on stage, fireworks exploding in front of him, his usual smile replaced by a look of determination.
Dubois, meanwhile, was greeted by jeers as he marched straight past the fireworks and towards the ring, wasting little time soaking up the occasion.
Actor Paddy Considine, comedian Rob Beckett, Oasis star Noel Gallagher and darts world champion Luke Littler were among the famous faces in attendance.

With 41 knockouts between the fighters, few expected the judges to be called upon. The feeling beforehand was that Wardley's best chance lay in making another fast start, having dropped Dubois inside the opening moments of their first meeting.
But in a stunning reversal, it took just 17 seconds for Wardley to hit the canvas as Dubois backed him into a corner and landed a straight right.
Chants of 'oh Fabio Wardley' were quickly silenced as Dubois continued to unload punishing combinations. Another furious attack towards the end of the round left Wardley in deep trouble.
Trainer Ben Davison, criticised for not withdrawing Wardley sooner in their first contest, stood poised with a towel in his hand as his fighter survived to the bell.
There had already been concerns over whether Wardley had returned too quickly after the punishment he absorbed in May, when he was left bloodied and badly swollen.

And those fears appeared justified as the challenger struggled to cope with Dubois' relentless pressure. Wardley's hands were low and his punches wild and telegraphed, lacking the menace he had shown in Manchester.
Backed into the corner again in the second round, he was subjected to another barrage before Davison leapt up and threw in the towel.

The two men could hardly be more different outside the ring. Dubois was typically reserved throughout fight week, looking uncomfortable in the media spotlight. Wardley, by contrast, was relaxed and articulate, insisting he had learned from his mistakes.
But despite their contrasting personalities and fierce rivalry, there was mutual respect at the end of the fight.
More to follow.

articles.headline: Daniel Dubois blows away Fabio Wardley inside two rounds of punishing rematch
keyFacts: Daniel Dubois defeated Fabio Wardley in two rounds to retain his WBO heavyweight title at London’s O2 Arena on Saturday night.
Dubois knocked Wardley down in the first round and continued his attack until Wardley's trainer Ben Davison threw in the towel in the second round.
Dubois stated he is now pursuing unification fights with other champions in the division.
body: Daniel Dubois made quick work of Fabio Wardley on Saturday night at London’s O2 Arena.
The defending WBO heavyweight champion needed just two rounds to dispatch Wardley in a frantic rematch that picked up right from where they left off in May.
Dubois steamrolled Wardley to retain his WBO heavyweight title Getty

Dubois sent Wardley tumbling to the canvas for the first time in his career in the opening stanza, and he hurt his rival badly again in the second as the Ipswich man’s trainer Ben Davison made the compassionate call to throw in the towel.
Wardley had been trapped in the corner under heavy artillery when the fight was waved off two minutes and twenty-one seconds into the frame.
Dubois and Wardley have their say
“Shout out to everybody, shoutout to my dad, my whole team,” said the victorious Dubois, who improves to 24-3.
“Fabio is a great warrior, but it was my time, my era.
“I had bad intentions from the beginning.
“Our back was against the wall the first time. We just had to go out there and show we meant business tonight.”
Humble as ever in defeat, Wardley added: “It’s never fun to lose.
“It is what it is, I’ve always thrown myself in with the biggest, toughest, meanest guys around; there’s no shame in testing yourself against the best.
“Daniel is a testament to coming again, and I’ll come again.
“You come with a game plan, try to adjust things, and it didn’t work tonight. It’s a credit to Daniel of how well he prepared.”
Wardley was never given a chance to get going by the brilliant Dubois Getty
Story of the fight
It was bombs away from the opening bell as Dubois decked Wardley inside the first 15 seconds with the first right hand he threw.
Wardley went down on one knee and popped back up again as referee Steve Gray stepped in and administered the count.
Dubois, smelling blood in the water, had to be wrestled away from Wardley as he continued to pour on the pressure after knocking his man down.
Wardley met the count, but wasn’t let off the hook, as Dubois went in relentless pursuit of the stoppage.
Davison was up on the apron at the end of the round, with his towel in hand.

articles.headline: Metal band Genitorturers allegedly claims a Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines remake is coming, getting a dozen crusty nerds way too worked up
keyFacts: A Reddit user reported that the metal band Genitorturers told a crowd in Brooklyn that a Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines remake is happening.
PC Gamer confirmed that Genitorturers played a show in Brooklyn on October 15, matching the timeline of the unverified rumor.
Commenters suggested the band may have confused the project with Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines 2 or acted on outdated information.
body: This one is thin, man, but it has to do with one of my favorite games of all time, while the circumstances of the rumor are just kind of neat and weird, even if it turns out to be nothing. User Few_Interview8222 on the Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines subreddit reported back from a Genitorturers show in Brooklyn, New York. Partway through the set, the band supposedly told the crowd that a VtMB remake is happening.

I haven't found any corroborating accounts of Few_Interview8222's story, but Genitorturers undeniably played at Brooklyn's The Meadows as part of their "Live + Lewd Tour" on October 15, which puts them in the right place at the right time. We've reached out to both rights-holder Activision (one of several, it's complicated) and Genitorturers' representation, and will update this story if we hear back.
Why would an industrial metal band started in Orlando in 1986 have this information?

In addition to a killer score by Rik Schaffer, Bloodlines featured wonderfully era-appropriate licensed tracks from metal bands—they were mostly used as diegetic music in the nightclubs and bars of Los Angeles. The Genitorturers track Lecher Bitch was the pitch-perfect theme of The Last Round, a downtown LA dive bar frequented by the Anarch faction of vampires.
What if they're wrong?

Multiple commenters on the Reddit thread point out that this could have been a confused, untimely, misinterpreted, or all of the above reference to last year's Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines 2. You could easily imagine a concertgoer mishearing something in that context, or a performer fumbling delivery of the exact information. It's the sort of almost-but-not-quite thing you might expect from an artist with tangential awareness of a secondary fanbase they picked up over the years.

A VtMB remake is also the sort of project you could see getting pingponged around between various actors and stakeholders: started, stopped, shopped around, etc. It'd be a situation ripe for collaborators on the periphery acting on outdated information.
What if they're right?

Rad! I think? It'd depend on who's doing it. More and more, I'm beginning to distrust anyone not named "Nightdive" when it comes to commercial remasters. See also: The recent Shogun 2 debacle and the fate of Deus Ex Remastered.

Bloodlines is such a wild, janky, PC gaming package that Nightdive is the only studio I'd trust to not only do a remaster right, but also to bring on legendary modder Werner "Wesp5" Spahl, the man who's been keeping Bloodlines alive with one of the most impactful unofficial patch projects in gaming. A more ground-up remake would offer equally daunting challenges, like matching the one-of-a-kind mood and look Troika managed to evoke.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
Why should you care?

Bloodlines is one of my very favorite games and an incredible RPG that's well worth your time. To the uninitiated, I like to pitch it as an evolutionary missing link between 2D Fallout and New Vegas. Bloodlines boasts the open-ended design and reactivity of Fallout in 3D for the very first time (Bloodlines leads Leonard Boyarsky and Jason Anderson were senior talent on Fallout 1).

Unlike New Vegas' wide open world, however, Bloodlines had a more linear, but still loose sequence of zones on a world map to explore. Bloodlines' Y2K, gothic, noir interpretation of Los Angeles is one of the coolest worlds ever presented in an RPG.

A Nightdive treatment would be my preferred outcome: build on Wesp5's work and compensate him accordingly, then make it more accessible on more platforms at a modest markup over the original game. Bloodlines 1 can be had for $20 on Steam and GOG, but it's practically always on sale.

Even if it turns out to be nothing, this is still just a neat, newsworthy little incident to behold—Genitorturers shouting out an obscure, beloved RPG like this 22 years later, and maybe getting a couple genre nerds like me a little too excited on the way.

Ted has been thinking about PC games and bothering anyone who would listen with his thoughts on them ever since he booted up his sister's copy of Neverwinter Nights on the family computer. He is obsessed with all things CRPG and CRPG-adjacent, but has also covered esports, modding, and rare game collecting. When he's not playing or writing about games, you can find Ted lifting weights on his back porch. You can follow Ted on Bluesky.

articles.headline: Rain98 is a blue-hued, pre-Y2K, Serial Experiments Lain inspired visual novel about time travelling to the past to end the world
keyFacts: Rain98 is a blue-hued, pre-Y2K visual novel demo about a suicidal present-day man who travels back to 1998 Tokyo.
The protagonist meets a depressed young woman named Reina Amehara, and the two strike up a deal to end the world.
According to the Steam page, the full game is scheduled to be released by the end of the year.
body: Picture this. You're me, and you boot up the demo for Rain98, an incredibly blue-looking, rainy visual novel set in Tokyo, 1998, about a woman who refers to herself as the Angolmois, a world-ending reference to the predictions of good ole Nostradamus. At one point you have to light this woman's cigarette in a lightly stylish sequence. You get to a bit where you're asked to put your name in, and you put it in because like its predecessors, this is surely a self-insert kind of situation. Only you get a Steam achievement for getting a game over for putting your name in. Rude! But curious, so you, and of course I mean I, pressed on.

In Rain98, you play as a nameless Generic Man who is deeply troubled, if not outright suicidal (of which this game has strong themes of) by the state of the world as it is in our present day. It's a fair stance to take! I would not exactly say things are good right now. But they weren't great in 1998 Japan, the year that Generic Man is somehow transported back to, finding this young woman, Reina Amehara, the Angolmois, in what he thinks is his apartment. She too is depressed about everything, and while the two don't hit it off at first, they strike up a deal: to end the world.

This Heisei-era ennui and nihilism is relatively appropriately placed too. It was a time of the lost decades, a period where Japan's economy massively stagnated, in turn influencing a wide range of strange, often anxiety-inducing and ominous works like Serial Experiments Lain, Neon Genesis Evangelion and All About Lily Chou-Chou. The first of the three is apparently an influence on Rain98, a touch you can certainly feel at least a little bit of in its vibe.

Quite quickly while playing the demo, I realised that this whole time travel situation is a pretty smart one. The world sucks now, and the world sucked then. How will these two characters from different parts of history respond to one another's inability to accept their material conditions, which aren't so different? That isn't an answer I found in the demo, I only managed about an hour of it and it runs a total of three hours, so I'm expecting to have to put a lot more than that into the full game.

Speaking of the full game, I didn't manage to experience all of what it has to offer either. There are seemingly a few different minigames scattered throughout, like one involving legally distinct DDR, legally distinct Tamagotchi, legally distinct Tekken, and more besides. Not sure if any of that can be found in the demo, but it all looks charming enough. I'm certainly won over by the demo so far, and if the Steam page sticks to its promises, Rain98 will be out by the end of the year.

articles.headline: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns
keyFacts: Meta updated its commercial terms to state it could use business account domain content to train AI models.
Legal experts expressed concern that the provision allowed Meta to scrape publisher websites for AI training.
Meta removed the language after stating the terms were meant only for ads and business products.
body: Meta recently updated its commercial terms of use, declaring that the company can “use any content from [a business account’s] domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of” Meta products and services.

According to legal experts interviewed by Nieman Lab, this looked like a “remarkable provision” that could give Meta permission to scrape the website of any publisher with a Meta business account and use the content to train the company’s AI models. (While Meta defeated a high-profile lawsuit over alleged copyright infringement last year, other cases against AI companies, including Meta, continue.)
However, a Meta spokesperson insisted that the updated terms did not reflect a change in the way Meta crawls the web. And now, The Verge reports that the provision has been removed.

“We’ve heard you and want to clarify: the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves,” the company said in a statement. “It does not change how Meta uses web crawlers.”

articles.headline: The Mortuary Assistant Film Director Jeremiah Kipp Passes Away
keyFacts: Underground horror director Jeremiah Kipp has passed away, as announced by his partner Lindsay Katt and The Long Island International Film Expo.
Kipp recently released his largest movie earlier in the year, which was an adaptation of the indie horror game The Mortuary Assistant.
According to Deadline, the director had just finished production on an upcoming horror feature based on Cambodian folklore titled Faceless.
body: Underground horror director Jeremiah Kipp has passed away, according to his partner Lindsay Katt. Confirmed through The Long Island International Film Expo, Kipp released his largest movie just earlier in the year, an adaptation of the hit indie horror game The Mortuary Assistant.
“Jeremiah was a gentle soul who was always generous with advice and sharing his knowledge of cinema,” writes the Film Expo, “he leaves behind many friends and an important legacy.”

Based on the 2022 video game, The Mortuary Assistant follows Rebecca (Kingdom Heartâs Willa Holland), a down on her luck woman hoping her new job will pave the road to recovery. Working grim but seemingly benign shifts at the morgue, she suddenly finds herself subject to strange visions. Thatâs when her employer, Raymond (Boardwalk Empireâs Paul Sparks), delivers the bad news. It seems a demonic spirit hitched a ride on one of the cadavers, and Rebecca will need to follow specific rituals to rid herself of the entity.

15 years ago Jeremiah Kipp made my dreams come true. I had a very dark and personal story about Suicide and he believed it needed to to be told. I got to write and produce "Crestfallen" as a film along side him. He became a mentor and a friend. Now he is gone and I am crushed. pic.twitter.com/bfc7ZBGQEo
— (NSC) The Beer Fridge (@PenningWyse) October 16, 2026

“Jeremiah brought his singular voice and passion to Dread through SLAPFACE and THE MORTUARY ASSISTANT,” posted the studio. “Our love and condolences are with Jeremiahâs family, friends, and collaborators.”

Shocked by his sudden passing, the New York horror movie community is mourning a man they describe as fostering with his time, passion and know-how. Before Assistant, Kipp filmed an array of indie nightmares, from shorts to Shudderâs Slapface in 2021. According to Deadline, the director had just wrapped production on Faceless, an upcoming horror feature based on Cambodian folklore.

The Mortuary Assistant was a crossover hit for publisher DreadXP, who had charmed indie scare fans with their Dread X collections but broke containment on the horror simulator hybrid. While it hasnât made as many waves as other recent adaptations like Iron Lung, it seems it performed well enough to assure the publisher. Elsewhere, DreadXP are expanding their cross-media operations, signing a deal with Blumhouse and YouTuber Matpat to adapt Amanda the Adventurer.

articles.headline: No further action against government adviser's wife over Palestine Action post, police say
